value.rationale: Fixed environmental switching can produce perfectly periodic mixed-frequency trajectories but the same fixed policy cannot make them attracting; the exact magnitude of instability is policy-period-dependent, monotonically and sharply. The universal residence-density derivation quantifies how time between switches trades fluctuation amplitude against robustness and supplies two explicit limiting exponents, even under asymmetric payoffs and duty fraction. It solves a motivated all-period structural question rather than a single tuned orbit or parameter computation. State-feedback, stochastic and multidimensional policies remain out of scope.
